3 major series, Enchanted Chronicles parodies fantasy, specifically Grimm and nursery rhyme tales, where the world runs on those sorts of rules but the bratty princess protag and her entourage are all about Lawyering up the loopholes, Regency Magic parodies turn-of-the-century school cliches like what Potter and The Worst Witch made popular, and Frontier Magic is a straight-up normal fantasy, but takes place in the unusual location of during the Gold Rush and Manifest Destiny eras.

Finally there's the wholly original World of Lyra series which she recommends you read a tiny bit out of order. If you're familiar with the Final Fantasy series of games, the setup is kind of like that as it has similar elements across each one but they're not fully related through character or location (or even time period).

Let's see. Here are my suggestions.

  • Neal Stephenson - Snow Crash, Diamond Age, and Cryptonomicon. All of them are pretty fun works of Sci Fi.

Snow Crash is an amusing deconstruction of the cyberpunk genre and is a great balance of humor, action, and things that make you think. It has seriously one of my favorite openings of any book ever.

Diamond Age is a bit more standard sci fi theme, with a good mix of action and statements/examinations of the role of class and culture in a near post-scarcity society.

Cryptonomicon is a corporate/spy thriller with a heavy focus on code breaking and encryption. If you're into information security at all, it's a great read.

  • Harry Turtledove - World War series, the Darkness Series, and the Southern Victory series. All of them are essentially alternate history retellings of World War II (and WWI as well in the Southern Victory series). Each with their own little twists.

World War involves a race of aliens invading Earth during the middle of WWII and the human nations in resistance attempts against them, despite the fact that they were/still are in a state of total war with each other.

The Darkness series is WWII retold in a fantasy world setting.

And the Southern Victory series is basically a retelling of WWI and WWII viewed through the lens of a fractured America where England and France had forced recognition of the Confederacy on the United States. It's probably the weakest of the series in my opinion, as he basically ignores the European conflict in favor of redoing everything they did, except they're Americans now.

  • David Brin's Uplift Universe is a series of books I'm currently really enjoying. They're all basically stand alone novels, although they do have a chronological progression. They're all about humanity's entrance into a Galactic Civilization which is dominated by the process of Uplift, where sentient species raise other species into sentience in a heavy ritualized fashion. The writing can be a bit weak at times, but the rich lore and alien design more than makes up for it, in my opinion.
